final.title: Know the demo limit before you automate
final.body:
If you have tried ChatGPT but have not connected it to a real workflow, the first question is not whether AI can answer a prompt. It is whether it fits one recurring task in your business without creating a bigger manual job around it. That is what demo limits are for: they draw the line between a proof of mechanism and a workflow you can actually run.

For a small business, the best candidate is usually a frequent, repeatable task with a measurable outcome, already living in English, email, docs, or SaaS tools. If you want a concrete frame, think of customer questions, lead follow-up, or invoice checking. The 8–10 hours a week example is only a persona scenario, not a market claim.

Our self-built demos show the mechanism, but only inside their own boundaries. The knowledge assistant works end to end locally on synthetic Acme Shop data and approved documents; the public route is locked. The accounts-payable demo can block duplicate invoices and require human-only approval for risky steps. It does not include OCR, billing, or multi-user operation, and it does not move money on its own. Computers are not good at hearing “trust me” and approving payments.

The practical next step is to check one workflow against three questions: is the output measurable, is the data already digital, and can a human approve the risky part? If yes, that is a sensible candidate for a diagnostic. If not, it is probably still too messy for automation.
